data.raw_text:
China’s Foreign Ministry has publicly warned Japan over its stance on the Taiwan issue. For example, Chinese spokesperson Lin Jian told Japan it must “stop playing with fire on the Taiwan question” and that “those who play with fire will perish with it”.  
In one instance, the Chinese consul­general in Osaka, Xue Jian, posted (then removed) a threat to “cut off that dirty neck without a second of hesitation”.  
This kind of language marks a marked escalation in tone: open threats, not just diplomatic protests.
Beijing recently summoned Japan’s ambassador in protest of remarks by Japan’s political leadership. According to a Chinese-language media source it was the first time Japan had made “a threat of force against China” and China demanded a correction by Tokyo. 
Japan is increasingly prominent in the US-led framework to deter Chinese aggression, especially in relation to Taiwan. China views Japan’s support for Taiwan or alignment with the US Indo-Pacific strategy as interference in its “core interests” (territorial integrity, One-China principle).
China’s sharp rhetorical escalation toward Japan is not an isolated diplomatic flareup. It is a structural manifestation of Cold War 2.0, where the DragonBear (China–Russia axis of stratetic coordination) is openly challenging the US-led Anglosphere alliance system. Japan, America’s pivotal Indo-Pacific ally, is now positioned at the front line of systemic confrontation. It is forward operating base of U.S. power projection into the First and Second Island Chains.
A logistical and political anchor for any U.S. Taiwan defense scenario and a rising defence actor shedding its post-war constraints.
China’s aggressive rhetoric such as “playing with fire” & “cutting off that dirty neck” is part of a deliberate campaign to intimidate Japan away from deeper coordination with the US, deter Japanese involvement in any Taiwan war scenario, and test the credibility of the US–Japan alliance, just as Russia tests NATO’s eastern flank.
This is the same playbook as Russia’s intimidation toward Poland/Baltics and China’s pressure on the Philippines.
Japan is now a primary friction node in Cold War 2.0 between America and the DragonBear and Taiwan is to China, what Ukraine is to Russia in strategic terms. Similarly to Iron Curtain 2.0 in Europe, in Cold War 2.0 terms, Taiwan is the Berlin of the Indo-Pacific now.
To win the Taiwan contest, China will further disrupt US logistics and use liabilities created by US dependencies on China; intimidate or neutralize US allies like Japan; create political division in them; raise the cost of involvement and weaken any cooperation formats under US legacy. 
This is also the DragonBear division of labor in real time.
Japan is no longer a secondary actor. It is becoming part of „the Eastern Flank“ of the Indo-Pacific - an industrial backbone, frontline state, and decisive theater for the future outcome of Cold War 2.0.
